questions.q: What are the four elements of the promotion mix as per the marketing mix (4 Ps)?
questions.a: The four elements are advertising, personal selling, sales promotion, and public relations. A wrong answer (e.g., including "direct marketing" or "packaging") reveals confusion between promotion mix components and other marketing mix elements or modern extensions not in the NCERT textbook.

questions.q: Explain why personal selling is more effective than advertising for selling complex, high-value industrial machinery.
questions.a: Personal selling allows two-way communication, demonstration, negotiation, and relationship building, which are crucial for complex, expensive products where buyers need detailed information and reassurance. Advertising is one-way and impersonal. A wrong answer that says "advertising is cheaper" misses the point that effectiveness depends on the nature of the product and buying situation.

questions.q: A company selling affordable daily-use shampoo wants to quickly increase trial among price-sensitive rural consumers. Which promotion tool should be the primary focus, and why?
questions.a: Sales promotion (e.g., free sachets, discounts, coupons) should be primary because it provides immediate incentive for trial, works well for low-involvement, low-price products, and reaches price-sensitive buyers. Advertising builds awareness but doesn't guarantee trial; personal selling is too costly for mass-market low-value items. A wrong answer choosing advertising shows inability to match tool to objective (trial vs awareness) and customer segment.

questions.q: Compare the cost per contact and feedback immediacy of advertising vs personal selling. Which is better for a new startup with limited budget targeting a niche B2B market?
questions.a: Advertising has low cost per contact but delayed/indirect feedback; personal selling has high cost per contact but immediate, direct feedback. For a niche B2B startup, personal selling is better despite higher cost because the target audience is small, identifiable, and requires relationship building. A wrong answer choosing advertising for B2B niche shows misunderstanding of target audience size and feedback needs.

questions.q: Critique the statement: "Public relations is free advertising because you don't pay for media space." Is this accurate? Why or why not?
questions.a: The statement is inaccurate. PR involves costs (agency fees, event organization, press kit production) and does not guarantee coverage or control over message, unlike paid advertising. "Free" refers only to not paying for media space, but the overall cost and uncertainty are high. A wrong answer agreeing with the statement reveals confusion between "no media buying cost" and "zero cost," and ignores the lack of control in PR.

questions.q: Design a promotion mix strategy for a new electric two-wheeler targeted at urban college students in India. Specify the role of each of the four tools and justify your choices.
questions.a: A good answer would include: Advertising (social media, influencer videos) for awareness and image building; Personal selling (test ride events at colleges) for experience and doubt clearance; Sales promotion (exchange offers, referral discounts) for immediate purchase incentive; Public relations (press releases on eco-friendly features, tie-ups with campus sustainability clubs) for credibility. Each tool's role must be justified by the target audience (students), product (high involvement, new technology), and budget constraints. A poor answer lists tools without linking to audience/product specifics.
